html:
The Philippines is an island country in Southeast Asia, made up of about 7,600 islands between the South China Sea and the Pacific. The map shows it from 1492 to 2010.

Before the Spanish came, people lived in barangays, communities led by datus. Trading towns such as Tondo, Cebu and Butuan dealt with China and the islands to the south, and in the south Islam had taken hold in the Sultanate of Sulu and Maguindanao.

Magellan reached the islands in 1521 and was killed at Mactan. Spain returned in 1565 and made Manila its capital in 1571, building the walled city of Intramuros. The islands were named after King Philip II and ruled through Mexico. Each year the Manila galleons carried Chinese silk and porcelain to Acapulco and brought back American silver. Friars made most lowlanders Catholic, while the Muslim south fought Spain for three centuries.

In the 1800s a Filipino educated class grew. Spain executed the writer José Rizal in 1896, the year the Philippine Revolution began. In 1898 Spain handed the islands to the United States for 20 million dollars, and the Philippine American War followed. Under American rule the country got self government in 1935, suffered Japanese occupation from 1942 to 1945, and became independent on 4 July 1946.

Ferdinand Marcos ruled under martial law from 1972. The peaceful People Power Revolution removed him in 1986.
sum: The Philippines is an island country in Southeast Asia, made up of about 7,600 islands between the South China Sea and the Pacific. The map shows it from 1492 to 2010.
